answer: Endorsement travels across a cut in the endorsement graph, and a cut is only real when the two sides have no common ancestor inside the endorsement horizon, so a cluster must be dissolved and rebuilt before its weight counts elsewhere. This cost is per identity, so it cannot be amortised across the fleet. The pigment is the island, the garden the endorsement that crosses it, and the cipher the shared ancestor that would disqualify the crossing; one pigment is cheap to hold, but a garden only counts when no cipher exists, and that takes independent history.
